newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS MUST DO WITHOUT DEL PIERO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS MUST DO WITHOUT DEL PIERO.

text.p: The last time Juventus played champions Milan in serie A, coach Marcello Lippi allowed himself the luxury of keeping Alessandro Del Piero on the bench until three minutes from the whistle.
When the two teams meet again on Sunday at San Siro, Lippi will not be able to rest any leading lights and injured attacker Del Piero will not even be there as a substitute.
To make matters worse, stand-in striker Michele Padovano injured his left thigh at training on Wednesday and will be out for a month.
Influential French midfielder Didier Deschamps is suspended as is Uruguayan defender Paolo Montero.

All will be missed as the European Cup holders aim to maintain a six-point lead over Parma at the top of the league. The last clash between Juventus and Milan in Turin in November ended in a thrilling, but goalless, draw.

"A lot hinges on Sunday's match and it would have been better to meet Milan a month ago, when they were still fighting to recover," said Italy defender Ciro Ferrara. "Now they are recovered, they are difficult."

Lippi has made a policy of rotating players and resting those showing signs of tiredness for fresher faces regardless of reputation. He has little choice against a resurgent Milan but to fall back on men with a busy week behind them.
The two-pronged attacking line-up is likely to be young Christian Vieri, who crowned his international debut on Saturday with Italy's 1,000th goal, and Croatia's Alen Boksic.
Both have played two World Cup qualifiers in a week with Boksic recovering from an injury suffered in January that sidelined him for more than a month.

Boksic is convinced, however, Vieri is now more confident than ever. "I think it's more important for him to have scored his first goal than Italy's 1,000th...now we'll get him back more charged up and more confident in himself."

Lippi had hoped that Del Piero, who pulled a thigh muscle in late February shortly after scoring his 50th goal for the club, would be recovered in time for Milan but it appeared that the 22-year-old has lost the battle.
"The lad has felt some new pain and we decided to rest him for three days," said club doctor Riccardo Agricola.
He said Del Piero had felt a sudden pain where the strained muscle had healed. The pain was not a serious worry but the niggle was enough to prevent him from playing.
Del Piero is also likely to miss the Ajax-Juventus European Cup semifinal first leg match next week but should return against Udinese on April 13.
Milan, in seventh place in the league 13 points behind Juventus, also have problems in attack as they try to continue a good run of form and chase a place in Europe.
"The 13 points gap shows clearly the difference in performance this season between the two," said defender Paolo Maldini.
"But not the difference in ability, which is clearly less. Milan have regained their style and confidence. We're not thinking of the title but beating Juve is always a pleasure."
Striker George Weah will be absent as Liberia are due to play Egypt in a World Cup qualifier on Sunday. Milan tried and failed to get that match played on Saturday.
There are also difficulties in defence, with Italy international Alessandro Costacurta suspended. Midfielder Demetrio Albertini is also absent due to injury.
Roberto Baggio, sounding increasingly frustrated at the club, is also likely to appear on the bench against a team with which he won the league title in 1995.
"I am wasting valuable time but what else can I do," Baggio lamented in Thursday's edition of Tuttosport. "At the moment it seems football is moving on without Roberto Baggio."
